problem: An explicit observation profile needs a deterministic complete manifest before a run and strict authentication before any copied runtime is loaded.
changes: ProfileBundle.materialized_manifest() computes the complete source-tree contract without I/O, and materialize_profile() uses that same contract.
verify_materialized_profile() requires explicit reviewed source and manifest hashes, rebuilds the expected contents using installed code, and authenticates the exact ordinary 16-file tree.
The verifier compares exact expected manifest bytes. Rehashing modified metadata, duplicate keys, nonfinite JSON or replacement runtime code cannot authorize a different profile.
Descriptor-based no-follow reads enforce file/count/byte bounds and stable identities; a final closed inventory must match. Returned bytes and identity data are immutable.
limits: Canonical Git verification remains a separate strict caller prerequisite; this library never claims to perform it.
The returned identity is not a filesystem lock. Callers must reverify before later imports and at lifecycle boundaries.
A helper source version change requires the corresponding new explicit manifest identity; old source trees receive no automatic fallback.
Benchmark, collector and admission dispatch are still pending. Existing corpora and model scores are unchanged.
The six browser cases use a fake policy and prove source integration and freshness behavior, not model quality or task success.
